summary: Over-segmentation failures mostly come from cutting between clauses that share an elided verb, a coreferential pronoun, or a parallel causative structure, which flips meaning or drops content. Under-segmentation failures are frequent and cheap to fix: leading discourse markers/fillers and mid-sentence punctuation (question marks, topic-shift connectives) are safe boundaries that were left unsplit, wasting available free latency. The prompt needs boundary rules keyed to clause completeness and shared referents/predicates, not just connective type.
